source: Ricardo's existing research page and October 2026 CV. Ongoing/past groupings are provisional and should be confirmed by Ricardo; the past Peixão entry covers the completed MSc phase, not all later collaborative work.
introduction: I use the chemical signatures of organic molecules to investigate past climate and environmental change. My work combines lipid biomarkers and compound-specific δ²H and δ¹³C measurements with other evidence preserved in lake sediments.
context: A central challenge is separating climatic signals from changes in the plants and aquatic organisms that produce the molecules we measure. I investigate these source effects through modern calibration studies and sedimentary records.

projects.title: Hydroclimate at Lake Rotsee
projects.summary: Separating vegetation effects from the hydroclimatic signals recorded by plant waxes in a Swiss lake.
projects.question: How can we distinguish changes in vegetation from changes in hydroclimate in sedimentary plant-wax isotope records?
projects.about: My work on Lake Rotsee examines how vegetation changes affect the hydrogen-isotope composition of sedimentary plant waxes. Vegetation-corrected reconstructions help assess the hydroclimatic information preserved across the transition from the Younger Dryas into the Holocene and through later environmental change.
projects.approach: Plant-wax δ²H and δ¹³C, lipid distributions, vegetation correction, and multi-proxy lake records.

projects.title: Postglacial hydroclimate at Owasco Lake
projects.summary: Investigating postglacial hydroclimate in the northeastern United States using vegetation-corrected plant-wax isotopes.
projects.question: How did the residual Laurentide Ice Sheet influence early Holocene hydroclimate in the northeastern United States?
projects.about: My ongoing work on Owasco Lake uses vegetation-corrected plant-wax isotope records to investigate postglacial hydroclimate in the northeastern United States, including early Holocene influences of the residual Laurentide Ice Sheet.
projects.approach: Plant-wax δ²H, vegetation correction, and sedimentary archives.

projects.title: Aquatic-plant lipid biomarkers
projects.summary: Understanding how charophytes and submerged vascular plants influence the lipid signals preserved in lake sediments.
projects.question: How do different aquatic plants contribute to the lipid and isotope signals used to reconstruct past environments?
projects.about: I compare the lipid signatures and hydrogen-isotope compositions of charophytes and submerged vascular plants. Understanding differences between these groups helps evaluate how changing aquatic communities influence the biomarker signals preserved in lake sediments.
projects.approach: Modern aquatic-plant lipids, compound-specific isotope analysis, and proxy calibration.

projects.title: Younger Dryas Working Group
projects.summary: Bringing together researchers and different climate archives to synthesize European evidence for the Younger Dryas.
projects.question: How can evidence from different European climate archives improve our understanding of the Younger Dryas?
projects.about: I am a co-initiator of the Younger Dryas Working Group, which brings together researchers working on lake records, speleothems, glaciers, chironomids, lipid biomarkers, and climate modelling to synthesize European evidence for this abrupt climate event.
projects.approach: Scientific exchange and synthesis across lake records, speleothems, glaciers, chironomids, lipid biomarkers, and climate modelling.

projects.title: Atlantic climate at Lake Peixão
projects.summary: Reconstructing western Iberian hydroclimate over the last 2,000 years from the sediments of a mountain lake.
projects.question: How have Atlantic climate variability, vegetation, and human activity shaped the environment around Lake Peixão?
projects.about: My MSc research used leaf-wax biomarkers from Lake Peixão in Serra da Estrela to investigate western Iberian hydroclimate over the last 2,000 years. This work examines connections between North Atlantic atmospheric circulation, local hydroclimate, vegetation, and human activity. The lake archive also supports collaborative studies of longer Holocene records.
projects.approach: Leaf-wax biomarkers, stable isotopes, pollen, and complementary sedimentary proxies.
